articles.title: My old teammate Miroslav Klose is bucking a trend in German coaching | Philipp Lahm
articles.summary: ‘Miro’, now in charge at Nürnberg, knows the value of consistency and identity in an era of tinkering coaches who did not play professionally. You learn the most from the best. The Champions League winners are Paris Saint-Germain, and they could achieve a historic hat-trick this season.
body: I see clear parallels between the two. For Madrid, nine players started in all three of their final victories. Similarly, PSG won their two finals with virtually identical lineups. The only change came during their title defence in Budapest, where Gianluigi Donnarumma no longer featured in goal, Luis Enrique having parted ways with the Italian European champion.

At its core, football has not changed. For two giants of the tournament’s predecessor, the European Cup – Ajax (1971 to 1973) and Bayern Munich (1974 to 1976) – seven players started all three finals. Had injuries not interfered, that number would have been higher. There is a similar pattern in Madrid’s five consecutive wins from 1956, with nine players appearing in at least three of those finals and three featuring in all five. Continuity plus selection: that is the eternal recipe for success.

articles.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
articles.summary: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club. Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point.
body: For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast.

But traducing the messenger will always be easier than hearing the message, even if Martínez’s views are widely shared within the United dressing room. If the fallout from the Manchester City legal case has demonstrated anything, it is English football’s ingrained reluctance to scrutinise the owners and executives who hold more influence over the sport than anybody else. articles.title: Brewers go one win from World Series as back-to-back homers sink Dodgers
articles.summary: Milwaukee rally past Los Angeles for 3-0 NLCS lead. Bauers and Mitchell homer back-to-back off Blake Snell. Defending champions face elimination on Thursday. Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back home runs off Blake Snell to reclaim the lead in the seventh inning as the Milwaukee…
body: The Dodgers had just taken a 2-1 lead in the bottom of the sixth before being stunned. The loss pushed the two-time defending World Series champions to the brink of elimination. They had trailed 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series only once previously in franchise history, when they were swept by the Baltimore Orioles in the 1966 World Series.

Snell had retired 14 consecutive batters entering the seventh. The two-time Cy Young Award winner’s first pitch of the game was driven out of the park by Jackson Chourio, and his last was Mitchell’s solo shot.

Andrew Vaughn drew a seven-pitch walk to open the seventh and was replaced by pinch-runner Christian Yelich. Bauers followed with a 412ft drive to right field on the 11th pitch of the at-bat, giving Milwaukee a 3-2 lead as much of the Brewers’ dugout spilled on to the field in celebration. Mitchell came up next and launched a 428ft shot to right-center, chasing Snell.
Snell allowed four runs on four hits over six-plus innings, striking out nine and walking two.

articles.title: Could Wenger really take on Infantino and run for Fifa presidency?
articles.summary: Senior figures in European football tell BBC Sport they want former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger to run as a surprise candidate against Gianni Infantino.
body: Despite the backlash caused by his failed plan to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors, Fifa president Gianni Infantino looks increasingly likely to be re-elected unopposed for a fourth and final term next year.
Senior figures within European football have told BBC Sport they want former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger to run as a surprise candidate.
But would the man who has been the governing body's head of global development since 2019 really challenge his own boss? And what lies behind the support he has?

On Thursday the Fifa Council will meet for the first time since the emergence of Infantino's Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme plunged the organisation into crisis, leading to calls from the game's leaders in Europe, North America and Asia for him to step down.

articles.title: From tear gas to just tears - rugby league's most passionate fans?
articles.summary: World Cup co-hosts Papua New Guinea's love of rugby league manifests itself in the Kumuls and the Orchids national teams, two badges of hope and unity for the island.
body: "Back home when we play in front of our own fans, just to see the fans, the crowd get behind us, singing the national anthem... it makes me cry every time."
Edwin Ipape gets emotional when travelling with his Papua New Guinea team-mates to the national stadium.

Children, so mad about rugby league that they will fashion a ball out of anything they can find, run alongside the team bus, eager to catch a glimpse of their heroes. Players are mobbed wherever they go.
The buzz around rugby league in Papua New Guinea can sometimes be daunting for visiting teams. In the past, passion has boiled over to the point where police have fired tear gas into the crowds.

articles.title: The time Souness rejected move from Liverpool to Barcelona
articles.summary: Liverpool legend Graeme Souness has revealed he rejected the chance to sign for Barcelona when he left the European champions in 1984. The Scotland midfielder joined Italian club Sampdoria for £650,000 just weeks after lifting Liverpool's fourth European Cup against Roma.
body: Souness was then one of the world's finest midfielders - he finished sixth in that year's Ballon d'Or - so his decision to swap Anfield for Genoa, rather than one of Europe's heavyweights, was a surprise.
"I had to leave Liverpool because my wife at the time was about to inherit money and she had to spend three years out of the country," Souness told BBC Scotland's The Saturday Show.
"I could have got around it somehow, but I decided to go because at that time Italy was the place to go. All the best players in the world were going there.
"I got offered a two-year deal at Barcelona, which I turned down because I needed three and, even because of my age, go to the third year.

articles.title: UEL | Salzburg vs Milan: Probable line-ups and where to watch on TV
articles.summary: Francesco Camarda and Fikayo Tomori are set to start for Milan as Ruben Amorim’s side visit Salzburg looking to recover from their opening Europa League defeat. It kicks off at 18:45 CET [17:45 BST] at the Red Bull Arena in Salzburg.
body: Milan were beaten at home by Benfica on Matchday 1, and they arrive in Austria after being held 1-1 by Sassuolo in Serie A at the weekend. Salzburg opened their campaign by beating Levski Sofia and are on a 15-game unbeaten run in all competitions, after a goalless draw with Grazer AK last time out.
Matteo Gabbia and Alexis Saelemaekers are unavailable for the Rossoneri, while Gonçalo Ramos is expected to drop to the bench after a heavy workload.

That opens the door for the young striker Camarda, who has played just eight minutes so far this season. It would be his first start of the campaign and his first in Europe. “Camarda? He’s an option against Salzburg, we have to give space to these young players,” Amorim said on the eve of the game.

According to Sky, Amorim will revert to a back three, with Tomori, Koni De Winter and Strahinja Pavlovic in front of Mike Maignan, and Adrien Rabiot is ahead of Luka Modric in midfield. The system could switch to a 4-2-3-1 or 4-4-1-1 during the game, with Tomori and Davide Bartesaghi as full-backs and Omari Hutchinson and Alphadjo Cisse pushed out wide.

articles.summary: Australia head coach Les Kiss has vowed the Wallabies will "return fire" against the All Blacks in Saturday's return Bledisloe Cup Test in Sydney, live on Sky Sports.
body: Last week, Australia's six-Test unbeaten run came to a shuddering halt when New Zealand ensured they will retain the Bledisloe Cup for a 24th year after powering to a 50-19 victory over the Wallabies at Eden Park.
A competitive first half, perhaps even edged by Australia, saw the All Blacks three points ahead at the break as the sides traded two tries each.
But the second half proved altogether different, as the All Blacks added five further tries in a display of clear dominance.
"It's like anything. You get a knockback, you find out more about yourself and that's what we'll do. We'll work hard on what we have to do," said Kiss.

articles.title: Man City beaten by PSG in thriller as Guardiola returns to Etihad
articles.summary: Manchester City were beaten 4-2 by a majestic Paris Saint-Germain as Pep Guardiola watched on from the stands in an enthralling Champions League encounter.
body: The reigning back-to-back European champions were keen to make their power felt early at the Etihad, in a game that made clear where the greater concentration of quality resides. Luis Enrique's side were breathtaking in the first half, a masterclass in effortless control with and without the ball.

Desire Doue scored from range. Ousmane Dembele rounded off a wonderful team move 99 seconds later. And Vitinha finished a brilliant first 45 minutes with a thumping finish from Warren Zaire-Emery's instinctive flick. "If you don't go toe-to-toe, you struggle," reflected Enzo Maresca.

A pair of Erling Haaland goals made the scoreline respectable after the interval, and City were good value for both breakthroughs, doing to PSG what had been done to them in the first period. They hit the woodwork a further two times in a half that became increasingly more frantic and transitional.

Despite wave after wave of attack and big chances missed, it was Gianluigi Donnarumma who failed to escape the glare of the spotlight, his poor handling gifting Maghnes Akliouche and the visitors a fourth. He atoned by denying Ferran Torres' woeful penalty attempt late on.
